terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: These terms govern use of the Bewegesund member platform.
items: Bewegesund provides educational movement, rehabilitation, and training content. It does not replace medical diagnosis, treatment, or emergency care.
You are responsible for entering accurate account and health-related information. Optional data helps personalize recommendations but can be added later.
If you experience acute pain, dizziness, chest pain, shortness of breath, neurological symptoms, or other warning signs, stop training and contact a medical professional.
Your account data is stored in Firebase and used inside the application for profile display, access control, training progress, and future recommendations.
Do not share your login credentials. You are responsible for activity performed through your account.
Programs, recommendations, and live sessions may change as the service develops.

breathingTechniques.title: 5 breathing techniques against stress
breathingTechniques.intro: Choose one technique, start the calm background music, and follow the steps at your own pace. Each exercise is short enough for everyday use and can be extended when needed.
breathingTechniques.musicNote: Soft music is generated for now

education.summary: Why these breathing techniques can help
education.title: Quick guide: breathing, nervous system, and relaxation
education.intro: This overview summarizes the background behind the five techniques. It is meant for users who want to understand why a breathing rhythm may feel calming, focusing, or supportive before sleep.

items.title: Quick Calm - prolonged exhalation
items.howItWorks: During exhalation, heart rate tends to slow. Extending the exhale can give the autonomic nervous system a signal of safety and support the shift from tension toward calm.

items.title: Deep Relaxation - diaphragmatic breathing
items.howItWorks: Stress often leads to shallow chest breathing. Moving the breath lower into the belly and diaphragm can reduce muscle tension and encourage parasympathetic activity.

items.title: Focus - box breathing
items.basis: Structured breath control in high-pressure performance
items.howItWorks: The steady pattern of inhaling, holding, exhaling, and holding gives the mind a clear anchor. Controlled breath holds can help stabilize breathing and build mental clarity.

items.title: Before Bed - the 4-7-8 method
items.howItWorks: The longer exhale and quiet pause between breaths slow the rhythm down. This method can help the body move from daytime alertness into a calmer pre-sleep state.

items.title: Free Slow Breathing - coherent breathing
items.howItWorks: A slow rhythm of about six breaths per minute can help breathing, blood pressure oscillations, and heart rate variability become more synchronized. Regular practice may support nervous system balance.

education.disclaimer: These breathing exercises are intended for general relaxation and wellbeing. They do not replace medical or psychological advice, diagnosis, or treatment. If you have cardiovascular issues, asthma, COPD, lung disease, severe anxiety or panic symptoms, are pregnant, or feel unsure, consult a physician first. Stop immediately if you feel dizzy, short of breath, or unwell.

sections.title: Quick Calm
sections.description: Prolonged exhalation for moments when you want to move out of inner tension quickly.
steps: Breathe in gently through the nose.
Exhale slowly for about six seconds.
Repeat the rhythm until your inner pace clearly slows.
sections.music: Music: very soft, slow, and without a strong melody.

sections.title: Deep Relaxation
sections.description: Diaphragmatic breathing to release shallow chest breathing and guide the body into a calmer state.
steps: Place one hand on the belly.
Inhale so the belly gently rises.
Let the exhale soften and flow out completely.
sections.music: Music: warm, deep, and evenly flowing.

sections.title: Focus
sections.description: Box breathing with a clear structure when you want to organize thoughts and become more focused.
steps: Count to four and hold the breath.
Count to four and exhale, then count to four and hold.
sections.music: Music: calm and rhythmic, with gentle pauses.

sections.title: Before Bed
sections.description: The 4-7-8 method as a quiet evening technique to prepare the body for sleep.
steps: Hold the breath for seven seconds without forcing.
sections.music: Music: especially quiet, warm, and without sharp highs.

sections.title: Free Slow Breathing
sections.description: Coherent breathing in a calm 5:5 rhythm for more steadiness in the nervous system.
steps: Stay close to about six breaths per minute.
sections.music: Music: low, flowing background with a stable pulse.
